clue.text: Get hold of some eggs

definitions.meaning: to seize or grasp something tightly
a batch of eggs laid at one time by a bird

explanation.surface: A farmer is told to collect a few eggs from the henhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for grasping firmly and a noun for a hen's set of eggs in one sitting.

clue.text: One in the right environment to get up late

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun, a morning spent in bed

indicators.note: the word for right forms a surrounding environment for the letter for one

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone in the right setting gets to sleep in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in the right environment' puts I inside LIEN; 'in the' is the link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A morning spent in bed past the usual hour is a late rising.

clue.text: Will try getting the last word at last

parts.note: to try something is to test it
amen is the last word of a prayer

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word at

explanation.surface: A legal will gets the final say in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: AMEN closes a prayer, hence 'the last word'.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a legal will disposing of one's property after death.

clue.text: Henry has a weapon in school

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A boy named Henry carries a weapon into school.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is an English private boarding school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow is a famous English public school, alma mater of Churchill.

clue.text: Count out diamonds-count for nothing

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word Count are thrown out of order

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player is told the diamonds in hand will not count at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'count' twice on purpose: first as fodder, then inside the definition, which is one idiom meaning to make no impression.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something that makes no impression or has no influence on anyone counts for nothing.

clue.text: Rite of passage when scoring a try?

definitions.meaning: the ceremony held on ships when sailors first cross the equator
in rugby a try is scored by grounding the ball over the opponents' goal boundary

explanation.surface: A rugby touchdown seen as a coming-of-age ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the equator ceremony for novice sailors and, in rugby, getting the ball past the goal boundary.

clue.text: Harmonious note swamped by sundry faults

indicators.note: swamped by means the note is engulfed by the rearranged letters
sundry suggests a mixed assortment, so the letters of faults are jumbled

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A harmonious musical note gets drowned out by various mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harmonious' looks musical beside 'note', but it is the definition in its sense of being in good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A tasteful design is pleasingly balanced and in good style, as a harmonious one is.

clue.text: Very good? A very good animal

parts.note: OK means all right, satisfactory
pi is short for pious, very good in the moral sense

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an animal is very good and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest mammal of central Africa, a relative of the giraffe.

clue.text: Flower in sweet bunch

parts.note: candy is a sweet
a tuft is a bunch of grass or hair

explanation.surface: A flower is found in a sweet-smelling bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Candytuft is a garden plant, Iberis, with clusters of white or purple blooms.

clue.text: Cut bits out of written promises, being hypercritical

parts.note: to censor a text is to cut parts out of it
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: An editor trims the paperwork of debt notes, being fussily critical.
explanation.definitionFit: A censorious person is severely fault-finding, quick to condemn others.

clue.text: Missing the first frequent connection

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to frequent a place is to haunt it

explanation.surface: A commuter misses the first of the regular train links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frequent' looks like an adjective but is the verb, giving HAUNT before its H goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A connection can mean a relative, and a father's or mother's sister is one such relation.

clue.text: I celebrated about noon — disgraceful!

parts.note: celebrated means famous, well known

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to partying around midday and is ashamed of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'celebrated' reads as a verb (I partied) but is the adjective FAMOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe conduct with a shameful reputation, notoriously bad.

clue.text: Fury and rage about state beginning to scrimp

indicators.note: about means the word for rage is turned round

parts.note: ire is anger or rage
NY is the abbreviation for New York, a US state

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word scrimp

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about the state of things when forced to economise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IRE into ERI. The capital on 'Fury' hides that it names one of the Furies of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Erinys is the Greek name for a single avenging goddess among the Furies.

clue.text: Profligate city without a name

indicators.note: without means the letter for name is taken away

parts.note: Rouen is a city in Normandy, France
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A dissolute man is found in an anonymous town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes N from ROUEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A debauched, dissipated man is a rake or libertine, and profligate as a noun means the same.

clue.text: Without help and love, nobody gets broadcast

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
none means no one
broadcast seed is sown, scattered widely

explanation.surface: Lacking help and love, nobody gets on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is not radio here: it means scattering seed, so SOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by oneself is doing it unaided.

clue.text: Submarine left America in pursuit of a unit that went adrift

indicators.note: in pursuit of means L and US come after the scrambled part
went adrift signals that the letters of a unit wander out of place

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: A lost military unit is chased by an American sub that departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went adrift' rearranges A UNIT as NAUTI, followed by L and US.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a famous submarine, Captain Nemo's vessel and later the first nuclear-powered sub.

clue.text: Noodles are often up the creek

definitions.text: Noodles are often up the creek

parts.words: Noodles are often up the creek
parts.note: noodles are often served in broth, and the phrase for that also means being in trouble

explanation.definitionFit: Being up the creek and in the broth both mean being in serious trouble.

clue.text: The available force of marines upset about damaged weapon

indicators.note: about means the reversed marines go round the jumbled weapon
upset in a down clue means the letters for marines are turned over

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of weapon are rearranged

explanation.surface: Marines are distressed about a broken weapon among the forces available.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down; 'about' and 'damaged' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Manpower means the number of workers or troops one can draw on.

clue.text: Shorten bridge

definitions.meaning: to make smaller or reduce in length
the card game in which a pledge to win tricks is made

explanation.surface: A two-word instruction to cut a bridge short.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to shrink; the noun is the variety of bridge played today, contract bridge.

clue.text: Skirt going over the top, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the entry sounds like a phrase

parts.note: too-too means excessive, overdone

explanation.surface: A skirt that is said to be extravagant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over the top' gives TOO-TOO, an old phrase for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina's short stiff frilled garment is a kind of skirt.

clue.text: Various people after pearls

definitions.meaning: an old word for several or sundry
those who go underwater looking for oysters

explanation.surface: Different people go looking for pearls.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an archaic adjective for several and the plural of one who dives.

clue.text: Some advocate acupuncture in the seat of the disturbance

definitions.text: in the seat of the disturbance

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone recommends needles as a cure for whatever is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the saying 'a storm in a teacup', a fuss over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm in a small china vessel is a petty row, so that vessel is where the disturbance sits.

clue.text: Metallic sound produced by a pound in coins

indicators.note: in means the pound sign goes inside the word for coins

parts.note: cash is money in coins
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A ringing sound is made by a pound coin dropping among others.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for pound, from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash is a loud jarring noise like cymbals striking.

clue.text: Newspaper man brought back in show proof

indicators.note: in means the reversed editor sits inside the word for show

parts.note: to evince is to show or display

indicators.note: brought back means the letters for the newspaper man are reversed

parts.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist returns to present the proof of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper man' is the usual crossword editor; 'show' is the verb, not a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts that establish the truth of something serve as confirmation of it.

clue.text: Cheddar adjudged superior to Edam, put in the first of each class

indicators.note: the first of each picks the initial letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A cheese judge rates Cheddar above Edam and places it top of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class in a rigid hierarchy.

clue.text: British island a part of America?

parts.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast

explanation.surface: A question of whether a British island belongs to America.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern state, so a component of the USA.

clue.text: Carving on a hillside in the Yukon

definitions.meaning: a figure of a pale steed cut into the chalk of an English down, like the one at Uffington
the capital city of Canada's Yukon territory

explanation.surface: A hill figure is found in the Canadian north.
explanation.walkthrough: Hill figures are horse shapes cut through turf into white chalk in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both chalk hill figures in England and the territorial capital of the Yukon.

clue.text: Reaching out, being responsible

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of Reaching are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stretching out a hand is taking charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges REACHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in command of something means being accountable for it.

clue.text: Very little money put into excellent meal

indicators.note: put into means the coin letter goes inside the word for excellent

parts.note: super means excellent
P is a penny, the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: A cheap but excellent dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for penny, the smallest British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening meal, a light dinner eaten late in the day.
